confidence_semantics: publisher/source authority only; not parcel numeric accuracy

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 per-tile metadata
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 supplies GEMINI XML metadata on a per-tile basis.
Metadata identifies product, grid/vector representation, 10 km National Grid tile reference and elevation topic context.
semantic_limits: Tile metadata is lineage/context, not a parcel elevation sample.
Per-tile metadata from the same OS product is correlated with the grid/contour data, not independent evidence.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 per-tile metadata
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 supplies per-tile GEMINI metadata including 5 km National Grid tile reference, British National Grid/vertical reference context, version and update lineage.
Lineage can state created from new imagery, partly revised, or verified with no change.
semantic_limits: Update lineage does not establish parcel-specific terrain uncertainty.
Styling statistics in auxiliary metadata are not parcel measurements.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 Technical Specification
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 is a bare-earth DTM supplied as 5 m grid points and 5 m contour data.
Grid and contour forms are generated from the same source data and supplied as 5 km tiles.
semantic_limits: Grid and contour forms are correlated views of one source model.
OS Terrain 5 remains a secondary cross-check to EA DTM1m for this workflow.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 Technical Specification
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 is a lower-resolution bare-earth DTM with 50 m grid spacing and 10 m contours.
Grid and contour products are created from the same source data and supplied as 10 km tiles.
semantic_limits: The 50 m product is coarse secondary evidence only.
Different file formats do not make independent measurements.

candidates.name: OS Terrain source TIN model
verified_facts: OS terrain source data is captured as a triangulated irregular network using mass points and breaklines or automated photogrammetric techniques.
Both grid and contour products are interpolated from the source TIN.
semantic_limits: TIN source accuracy requirements are not automatically the same as published product or parcel accuracy.
Grid and contour agreement is correlated because both derive from the same TIN.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 grid data structure
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 ASCII grid heights are calculated from pixel centres on a 50 m by 50 m raster grid.
GML alongside the ASCII grid provides location, grid spacing, vertical-reference and spatial-reference metadata rather than a separate height block.
semantic_limits: A 50 m pixel-centre value is a coarse cross-check and not an exact parcel extremum.
The GML metadata wrapper is not an independent elevation observation.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 spot-height semantics
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 spot heights are algorithmically selected from source data inside enclosed contours.
OS states such spot heights cannot be guaranteed to represent summits or the highest point of a real-world feature.
semantic_limits: Spot heights must not substitute for parcel min/max extraction.
A spot height is correlated with the same terrain source and is not independent validation.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 contour data model
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 contours are supplied in GML and include a separate metadata file.
Spot-height z values in contour supply are rounded to zero decimal places.
semantic_limits: Rounded contour spot heights are unsuitable for precise parcel height differences.
Contour metadata and contour geometry remain secondary corroboration only.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 grid external height block
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 GML does not itself contain spatial height data; the ASCII grid is the external data block containing heights.
The GML provides location, grid spacing, vertical reference and software-independent spatial-reference metadata.
semantic_limits: Reading only the GML metadata cannot produce a valid height value.
Metadata and ASCII from the same tile are components of one product, not independent sources.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 product supply and update schedule
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 national supply is organised into 5 km tiles and is updated quarterly in January, April, July and October.
Tile-level metadata files accompany the product supply.
semantic_limits: Publication cadence does not equal survey date for a parcel.
Tile packaging does not imply parcel-level accuracy.

candidates.name: HM Land Registry plans: boundaries practice guide 40 supplement 3
verified_facts: Updated 1 June 2026, the guide states the great majority of registered titles use general boundaries.
HMLR states there is no standard tolerance, measurement or ratio linking a general title-plan boundary to the exact legal boundary.
semantic_limits: General-boundary geometry cannot be promoted to exact legal-boundary precision.
OS mapping tolerances do not become HMLR general-boundary tolerances.

candidates.name: HM Land Registry plans: title plan practice guide 40 supplement 5
verified_facts: Updated 13 July 2026, HMLR states title plans graphically identify the general extent and must be read with the register.
All title plans show general boundaries unless the relevant boundary line is recorded as determined under section 60 of the Land Registration Act 2002.
semantic_limits: Title-plan dimensions or red edging do not by themselves prove the exact legal line.
Title plan geometry is horizontal property evidence, not terrain elevation evidence.

candidates.name: Boundary agreements and determined boundaries practice guide 40 supplement 4
verified_facts: Updated 1 June 2026, HMLR distinguishes general boundaries from determined boundaries.
A determined boundary records the exact line after that line has been identified, with explicit register and filed-plan evidence.
semantic_limits: Exact-boundary status requires explicit determined-boundary evidence; it cannot be inferred from INSPIRE or ordinary title-plan geometry.
Determined horizontal boundary evidence still does not supply terrain height values.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model 2m
verified_facts: EA describes the 2022 2 m Composite DTM as a bare-earth raster built from Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat surveys exist the newest/best resolution source is used, and resampling can use bilinear interpolation; EA directs users to metadata indexes for the contributing survey at a location.
semantic_limits: The 2 m composite is not a substitute for the workflow's primary 1 m DTM sample.
Composite publication date does not identify the parcel-specific source survey without metadata-index matching.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Surface Model 1m
verified_facts: EA describes the Composite DSM as including terrain plus objects such as vehicles, buildings and vegetation.
The DSM is assembled from Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys and uses the metadata catalogue for source lineage.
semantic_limits: DSM is excluded from bare-earth parcel extrema.
DSM lineage may corroborate survey provenance but cannot replace DTM sampling.
